{{short description|German-Jewish mathematician}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''Theodor Estermann''' (5 February 1902 – 29 November 1991) was a German-born British [[mathematician]], working in the field of [[analytic number theory]]. The [[Estermann measure]], a measure of the [[central symmetry]] of a [[convex set]] in the [[Euclidean plane]], is named after him.<ref>{{cite book
 | last = Grünbaum | first = Branko | author-link = Branko Grünbaum
 | editor-last = Klee | editor-first = Victor L. | editor-link = Victor Klee
 | contribution = Measures of symmetry for convex sets
 | location = Providence, Rhode Island
 | mr = 0156259
 | pages = 233–270
 | publisher = American Mathematical Society
 | series = Proceedings of Symposia in Pure Mathematics
 | title = Convexity
 | volume = 7
 | year = 1963}}</ref>

He was born in [[Neubrandenburg]], [[Germany]], "to keen [[Zionists]] who named him in honour of [[Theodor Herzl|Herzl]]."<ref>[[William D. Rubinstein]], Michael Jolles, [[Hilary L. Rubinstein]], ''The Palgrave Dictionary of Anglo-Jewish History'', Palgrave Macmillan (2011), p. 260</ref> His doctorate, completed in 1925, was supervised by [[Hans Rademacher]]. He spent most of his career at [[University College London]], eventually as a [[professor]]. [[Heini Halberstam]], [[Klaus Roth]] and [[Robert Charles Vaughan (mathematician)|Robert Charles Vaughan]] were Ph.D. students of his.

Though Estermann left Germany in 1929, before the [[Enabling Act of 1933|Nazis seized power]] in 1933, some historians count him among the early emigrants who fled Nazi Germany.<ref>{{Cite book |publisher=Princeton University Press |isbn=978-0-691-12593-0 |last=Siegmund-Schultze |first=Reinhard |title=Mathematicians Fleeing from Nazi Germany: Individual Fates and Global Impact |date=2009 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=jBoEmGB3B3MC |page=8}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Pinl |first1=Max |last2=Furtmüller |first2=Lux |title=Mathematicians under Hitler |journal=The Leo Baeck Institute Year Book |volume=18 |issue=1 |doi=10.1093/leobaeck/20.1.370 |date=1973}}</ref>

The physicist [[Immanuel Estermann]] was the brother of Theodor Estermann.
